goal.source_text: More downforce without going over 15 N of drag at 25 m/s. You can change the angle, span, flap angle, flap size and endplates. Keep the chord.
assumptions: Chord, airfoil, mounts and ride height stay fixed.

design_space.name: FSAE-style rear wing

parameters.name: chord_mm
parameters.description: Total chord, main element plus flap

parameters.name: flap_chord_frac
parameters.description: Flap chord as a fraction of total chord

notes: Ranges from PLAN.md B.5; W-B owns the real solver and may narrow them before CP-B.

metric_catalog.name: downforce_n
metric_catalog.description: Downforce at the design speed (VLM + viscous correction + endplates)

metric_catalog.name: drag_n
metric_catalog.description: Total drag: induced + section profile + endplate friction

metric_catalog.name: drag_profile_n
metric_catalog.description: Section profile drag (NeuralFoil) plus endplate skin friction

metric_catalog.name: cl
metric_catalog.description: Wing lift coefficient on planform area

metric_catalog.name: stall_margin_deg
metric_catalog.description: Section stall angle minus angle of attack (negative = stalled)

metric_catalog.name: span_efficiency
metric_catalog.description: Oswald e from Prandtl lifting-line theory for the planform

payload.rationale: Drag is 11.3 N against a 15.0 N cap, so span—the most drag-efficient downforce lever—plus taller endplates to cut induced drag is the safe first move. Bracket both.

payload.explanation: Both levers raised downforce 15.5% and L/D 11.7%, with drag up only 3.38% to 11.7 N, so the step was accepted. Induced drag fell 3.12% as aspect ratio rose 23.6%, but profile drag jumped 27.9%, far above the 5–14% forecast, because the taller endplates add wetted area; L/D still beat its 2–8% range.
payload.lesson: For this wing, span plus taller endplates is an efficient downforce move; profile drag rises with endplate wetted area.

payload.lesson: Near stall, extra AoA can cut downforce and spike profile drag; watch stall margin before adding angle.

payload.explanation: Prediction failed: lowering flap 15→12° and raising AoA 6→7° cut downforce 3.74%, not raised it; drag fell 9.44%, so L/D rose 6.30%. The flap reduction dominated, cutting profile drag 15.9% and induced drag 7.33% while CL fell 3.74%; stall margin stayed 3.5°.
payload.lesson: Near flap saturation, flap angle dominates downforce; trading flap for AoA loses lift despite lower drag.

payload.explanation: The 0.36→0.38 flap-chord step barely moved downforce (+0.132%) and drag (+0.784%), missing the predicted 1.5-5% gain; L/D fell 0.647% and stall margin held. The extra drag was mostly profile (+2.375%, induced +0.263%), so the accepted design gains little downforce at a small efficiency cost.
payload.lesson: Flap chord near 0.36-0.38 is a weak downforce lever, adding mostly profile drag; avoid it for downforce gains.

Stall margin dropped 14.3% to 3.0 deg and L/D fell 6.27%, so the flap is already past useful camber, causing separation-like penalties rather than extra lift.
